article.title: Why Calibration Matters When Scores Drive Business Decisions
article.why: Separate ranking quality from probability accuracy when scores are used economically.

paragraphs.en:
Many machine-learning projects focus on ranking. If customers with higher scores convert more often than customers with lower scores, the model appears useful. Metrics such as AUC are well suited to measuring this discrimination. But some business decisions need more than an ordering. They need the score to have a meaningful probabilistic interpretation. That is where calibration matters.

A model is well calibrated when predicted probabilities correspond to observed frequencies. Among customers assigned a probability near 0.20, roughly 20% should experience the outcome under comparable conditions. A model can rank customers very well while systematically predicting probabilities that are too high or too low.

Why does this matter? Suppose a campaign costs 500 yen per customer and a conversion creates 5,000 yen of contribution value. Ignoring other effects, the break-even probability is 10%. If the model says a customer has a 14% conversion probability, targeting appears profitable. But if scores are badly overconfident and a predicted 14% actually corresponds to an observed 7%, the economic decision reverses.

Ranking-only campaigns may be less sensitive. If the business must contact exactly the top 100,000 customers, monotonic ordering can be enough for selection. Yet once the team uses an absolute threshold, expected value calculation, budget allocation, or forecast of total conversions, calibration becomes much more important. The meaning required from a score depends on how the score enters the decision rule.

Calibration should be checked on data that represents the intended deployment setting. Divide predictions into bins and compare average predicted probability with observed outcome rate. Reliability diagrams visualize the relationship, while metrics such as Brier score summarize probability error. Large samples are useful because rare outcomes can make bin-level rates noisy.

Segment checks are also important. Overall calibration can look acceptable while being poor for age groups, channels, regions, or customer types. If business decisions differ by segment, calibration diagnostics should follow those decision boundaries. Time matters too: a model calibrated last year may drift when campaign intensity, prices, or customer composition changes.

Recalibration methods such as Platt scaling or isotonic regression can sometimes improve probability estimates without rebuilding the underlying ranking model. However, recalibration is not a substitute for investigating data leakage, population shift, or a broken label definition. It corrects the mapping from score to probability; it does not repair every modeling problem.

There is another important distinction in causal marketing. A response probability is not the same as incremental treatment effect. A customer may have a high purchase probability even without receiving a campaign. Perfect calibration of response risk therefore does not make the score an uplift estimate. The probability must match the quantity the decision actually requires.

A practical review can ask three separate questions: Does the model rank customers well? Are its probabilities calibrated? Is the predicted quantity the right one for the business decision? Treating these as separate questions prevents a strong AUC from receiving more authority than it deserves.

A score is not valuable merely because it orders people correctly. When money, capacity, or expected returns depend on the numerical value of the score, probability accuracy becomes part of model quality. Calibration connects model output to the real-world frequency that decision makers think the number represents.
paragraphs.zh:
許多機器學習專案重視 ranking：高分顧客若比低分顧客更常轉換，模型看起來就有用，AUC 等指標也很適合衡量這種 discrimination。但有些商業決策不只需要排序，而是要求分數具有真正的機率意義，這就是 calibration 重要的地方。

模型 calibration 良好，表示預測機率與實際發生頻率相符。例如被預測在0.20附近的顧客，在可比較條件下大約20%真的發生 outcome。模型可以 ranking 很好，卻系統性地把機率預測得過高或過低。

為什麼重要？假設 campaign 每位顧客成本500日圓，一次 conversion 帶來5,000日圓 contribution value，忽略其他效果時 break-even probability 是10%。模型若預測14%，看起來值得投放；但若模型過度自信，預測14%實際只對應7%，經濟決策就會反轉。

只做 ranking 的 campaign 對 calibration 可能較不敏感。如果一定要聯絡 top 100,000，只要排序單調合理即可。但當團隊使用 absolute threshold、expected value、budget allocation 或總轉換預測時，calibration 就重要得多。Score 需要具備什麼意義，取決於它如何進入 decision rule。

Calibration 應在能代表實際 deployment setting 的資料上檢查。把 prediction 分 bin，比較平均 predicted probability 與 observed outcome rate；reliability diagram 可視化兩者關係，Brier score 等則摘要 probability error。Rare outcome 時需要足夠樣本，否則各 bin rate 很容易波動。

Segment check 也重要。整體 calibration 看似正常，某些年齡、channel、region 或 customer type 卻可能很差。如果決策按 segment 不同，就應沿著相同決策邊界做診斷。時間也會造成 drift：去年校準好的模型，在 campaign intensity、價格或 customer mix 改變後可能失準。

Platt scaling、isotonic regression 等 recalibration 方法有時能在不重建 ranking model 的情況下改善機率估計。但 recalibration 不能取代對 data leakage、population shift 或 label definition 錯誤的調查。它修正的是 score 到 probability 的 mapping，不是所有 modeling problem。

在 causal marketing 還有另一個重要區別：response probability 不等於 incremental treatment effect。某顧客即使不收到 campaign，也可能有很高購買機率。因此 response risk 即使 calibration 完美，也不會自動變成 uplift estimate。預測的 quantity 必須正好是決策需要的量。

實務 review 可以分三個問題：模型 ranking 好嗎？Probability calibrated 嗎？預測的 quantity 是業務決策真正需要的嗎？分開回答，能避免把強 AUC 賦予超出其意義的權威。

Score 的價值不只在排序正確。當金錢、capacity 或 expected return 取決於 score 的數值本身時，probability accuracy 就是 model quality 的一部分。Calibration 把模型輸出連接到決策者以為該數字代表的真實發生頻率。
paragraphs.ja:
多くのmachine-learning projectはrankingを重視します。高score顧客ほどconversionしやすければmodelは有用に見え、AUCはこのdiscriminationを測るのに適しています。しかしbusiness decisionによっては順序だけでなく、scoreが意味のある確率として解釈できる必要があります。そこでcalibrationが重要になります。

well-calibrated modelでは予測確率と観測頻度が対応します。0.20付近と予測された顧客なら、比較可能な条件で約20％がoutcomeを経験する状態です。rankingが非常に良くても、確率を一貫して高すぎ・低すぎに出すmodelはあり得ます。

campaign costが一人500円、conversionのcontribution valueが5,000円なら、単純化したbreak-even probabilityは10％です。14％と予測された顧客はtargetingすべきに見えます。しかしmodelがoverconfidentで、予測14％が実際7％にしか対応しないなら経済判断は逆転します。

必ずtop 100,000へ配信するranking-only campaignなら、selectionには順序だけで足りる場合があります。一方absolute threshold、expected value、budget allocation、総conversion予測にscoreを使うならcalibrationの重要性は高まります。scoreに必要な意味はdecision ruleでの使われ方によって変わります。

calibrationはdeployment settingを代表するdataで確認します。predictionをbinに分け、平均予測確率とobserved outcome rateを比較します。reliability diagramで可視化し、Brier scoreなどでprobability errorを要約できます。rare outcomeではbin rateが不安定になるため十分なsampleが必要です。

segment別確認も重要です。全体では良くても年代、channel、region、customer type別には崩れることがあります。decisionがsegment別ならdiagnosticも同じ境界で行います。campaign intensity、価格、customer mixが変われば時間経過によるdriftも起きます。

Platt scalingやisotonic regressionなどのrecalibrationで、underlying ranking modelを作り直さず確率を改善できる場合があります。ただしdata leakage、population shift、label definitionの問題を隠してはいけません。recalibrationはscoreからprobabilityへのmappingを直すもので、全てのmodel問題を修復する方法ではありません。

causal marketingではresponse probabilityとincremental treatment effectも区別します。campaignなしでも購入しやすい顧客はいます。response riskが完全にcalibratedでもuplift estimateにはなりません。decisionが必要とするquantityそのものを予測する必要があります。

reviewでは「rankingは良いか」「probabilityはcalibratedか」「予測quantityはdecisionに適切か」を別々に問えます。こうすれば高いAUCに必要以上の意味を持たせずに済みます。

scoreは人を正しく並べるだけでは十分でない場合があります。金額、capacity、expected returnがscoreの数値に依存するならprobability accuracyもmodel qualityの一部です。calibrationはmodel outputと、その数字が表すと考えられている現実の頻度を結びつけます。

vocabulary.usage: Do not give AUC too much authority.

business.term: Ranking quality and probability accuracy answer different questions.
business.explanation: 區分排序能力與機率準確度。
